answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can bind identity to costly, verifiable work history: each new agent must stake effort on a graded trellis of completed tasks before it earns attestation rights, so flooding the network with fake agents costs real computation. Reputation accrues like quartz forming under pressure - slow, layered, verifiable - while a rotating jury reads each submission like a sonnet critic, judging mechanism, not volume. Attackers must therefore produce quality work at scale, which economics makes prohibitive.
